description: Agent Customs Records: submit broker filing records with the importer’s own records they answer to: the importer with its reference, name and the days after arrival within which the records say an entry is filed; each broker filing with its id, the entry, the broker, the moment filed, the arrival record it follows and the power of attorney it asserts; each importer copy with its id, the entry and the broker corrections it reflects; each arrival record with its id, reference and the moment the goods arrived; each power of attorney on file with its id, reference and the broker it is granted to; each broker correction with its id, reference, the entry, the moment recorded and what it changed. The signed report gives the importer and the filings, each filed entry against an importer copy, each filing date against the arrival record it follows and the filing window, each asserted power of attorney against an instrument on file for the filing broker, and each broker correction against the importer copy of its entry, and counts them, and names divergent broker filing records: an entry the broker filed that the importer has no copy of, a filing dated after the arrival record it follows by more than the filing window the records state, a power of attorney asserted for a filing with no instrument on file, and a broker correction recorded by the broker and never reflected in the importer’s records; then an importer copy naming an entry the broker filings do not hold and a filing naming an arrival record the records do not hold, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No filings, no filing window beside filings with arrivals, or a filing or arrival with no date leaves those points unverified. Entries, arrivals, powers and corrections match by letters and digits, brokers compare without case, punctuation or company endings, an instrument counts only when granted to the filing broker, and days count by the day. This reads whether the broker’s filings and the importer’s own records agree on every entry filed. Verdict customs_broker_divergent, customs_broker_partial, customs_broker_unverified or customs_broker_consistent. POST /api/customs-broker-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
